Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-cf69f9ec: closed rectangular frame fill

## When to Use
Use on task-cf69f9ec instances with color-5 rectangular scaffolds on color-9 background.

For task id `task-cf69f9ec`, inspect the color-5 scaffold on background 9. Fill the strict interior of fully closed rectangular frames with color 4; preserve every color-5 border and all other cells, including open/incomplete frame-like structures.

## Evidence from a solved instance

Input was 15x22, background 9 and frame color 5. Three closed rectangles were present:
- rows 3–7, columns 8–14: strict interior rows 4–6, columns 9–13 turned to 4 (3x5).
- rows 3–7, columns 14–21: strict interior rows 4–6, columns 15–20 turned to 4 (3x6). Shared border at column 14 remains color 5.
- rows 9–14, columns 8–12: strict interior rows 10–13, columns 9–11 turned to 4 (4x3).
All other scaffold cells and background stayed unchanged. First two frames share a vertical wall; treat each as a separate closed enclosure.

## Important distinction
A scaffold that looks almost rectangular but has an absent side/open perimeter must not be filled. In this instance, rows 9–12, columns 8–12 had top and partial vertical sides but was not closed; it remained entirely color 5/9. Isolated or dangling color-5 lines are untouched.

## Procedure
1. Identify axis-aligned color-5 rectangular perimeters with all four sides continuously present.
2. For each closed rectangle, recolor only strict interior cells (excluding perimeter) to 4.
3. Leave open frames, other color-5 marks, and all 9s outside interiors unchanged.
4. Check shared walls carefully: they remain 5, while each adjacent closed rectangle's strict interior is filled independently.

# task-42a90bbc: expand inner color around rectangle

## Observed demonstrations
Inputs contain a solid rectangular plate of one color, with a smaller contrasting patch (or singleton) inside; the rest is color 0. Outputs preserve the original rectangle and its internal patch, and add a larger rectangular border/plate of the internal patch's color outside the original rectangle. Background remains 0 outside that expanded shell.

- Demo 1, input 13x19: color-4 rectangle rows 2–9, cols 2–8 (8x7); inner color-5 patch rows 4–7, cols 4–6 (4x3). Output keeps those cells and extends color 5 as a shell/envelope, bbox rows 0–11, cols 0–10: top/bottom two rows across cols 0–10, plus two-cell side bands on rows 2–9. Rest unchanged 0.
- Demo 2, input 13x14: color-3 rectangle rows 3–7, cols 3–7 (5x5), with a single color-1 cell at (5,5). Output keeps it and adds color 1 one cell beyond all four edges: bbox rows 2–8, cols 2–8, one-cell top/bottom and side bands. Rest 0.
- Demo 3, input 15x14: color-6 rectangle rows 3–6, cols 3–6 (4x4), inner color-4 patch rows 4–5, cols 4–5 (2x2). Output keeps it and adds color 4 as a two-cell shell, bbox rows 1–8, cols 1–8. Rest 0.

## Strongly supported rule
Take the inner contrasting color and propagate it outside the plate as a full rectangular outer shell/frame surrounding the plate; preserve the original plate and inner patch exactly. Do not recolor the entire expanded rectangle uniformly: the interior/base rectangle remains its original color except for its existing inner patch. Preserve zero outside the shell.

The shell thickness varies by instance (demo2 = 1, demos1/3 = 2). Available evidence does NOT establish a reliable general formula for thickness. Do not blindly infer a fixed thickness or use the CF69 closed-frame task rule. Request an additional demo aimed at a different inner-patch shape/size if resolving thickness is necessary; compare shell expansion distances against inner patch size and margins.

## Test geometry from one failed instance
Test outer color-3 square: rows 6–11, cols 5–10 (6x6); inner color-8 square rows 7–10, cols 6–9 (4x4); all else 0 (21x21). No correct answer was obtained before cap. A submitted candidate added a 2-cell color-8 shell at rows 4–13/cols 3–12, while preserving the original 3 frame and 8 center; it was marked incorrect. Other failed candidates included 1-cell shell, 3-cell shell, and larger/offset shells. Thus the desired shell is NOT any of those exact submissions; don't reuse them. Most likely revisit thickness criterion using demos/further evidence rather than guessing again.

## Failed submissions caution
The same test was repeatedly submitted with differing wrong shells: coarse 2-cell expansion candidates, 3-cell and 1-cell expansions, and an overlarge/offset expansion. All incorrect (7 wrong submissions total, then one more wrong final submission). The rule's broad color relationship is supported, but location/extent/thickness formula remains unresolved. On a future recurrence, spend a demo request before committing to a speculative shell; test the proposed formula against all three demos AND the 6x6 test geometry.
